terms.meaning: A voluntary body started by weaker sections to serve its members as equals.
A business created by law, with a separate legal entity, perpetual succession and a common seal.
A company that owns and runs business in two or more countries, controlled from one head office.
A government undertaking that gives essential services without aiming at profit, such as water or railways.
A market where shares and debentures of listed companies are bought and sold.

items.name: The first co-operative society
items.formula: Started in 1844 at Rochdale in England, a consumer society; the book credits Robert Owen.
items.example: Farmers' credit societies free them from moneylenders.

items.name: Features of co-operative societies
items.formula: Voluntary, open to all adults, one member one vote, government supervision.
items.example: Profit shared, not less than 6.25%, with a part to the general fund.

items.name: Merits and demerits of co-operatives
items.formula: Merits: easy to form, little capital, limited liability, savings habit.
items.example: Demerits: limited capital, mismanagement, corruption and favouritism.

items.name: Co-operative movement in India
items.formula: Began with the Act of 1904; the 1912 Act made registration compulsory.

items.name: Co-operatives in Karnataka
items.formula: The first was at Kanaginahala in Gadag; Bengaluru City Central Co-operative society began in 1905.
items.example: Dharwad district is called the cradle of the co-operative movement.

items.name: Joint stock companies
items.formula: Governed by the Companies Act of 1956; owned by shareholders in proportion to their shares.
items.example: Haney: capital divided into transferable shares.

items.name: Features of MNCs
items.formula: Very large, in at least six countries, central control, big role in international trade.
items.example: Born as early as 1860, popular after the Second World War; first in the USA.

items.name: Examples of MNCs
items.example: Indian MNCs: Tatas, Birla, Infosys, Wipro; many came after liberalisation in 1991.

items.name: Disadvantages of MNCs
items.formula: Home country takes most profit; monopoly, tax avoidance, exploiting labour in host countries.

items.name: Government and joint sector undertakings
items.formula: Government: run by a ministry (mining, ship building). Joint sector: public and government together (Gujarat Fertilizers, Cochin Refineries).
items.example: Public utilities aim at service, not profit.

items.name: India's stock exchanges
items.formula: The first was in Mumbai in 1875.

mistakes.text: In a co-operative each member has one vote however many shares they hold; in a company, ownership follows shares.
The first Karnataka co-operative was at Kanaginahala (Gadag), but Dharwad district is called the cradle of the movement.
Public utilities don't aim to earn profit, unlike companies.
